advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add enrichment assertions for broken_oracle (must stay) and incomplete_enumeration (must clear to 'none'), plus a non-referencing-finding case that leaves attrs untouched.
evidence: Test only asserts: `attrs["ac_unverifiable"] == "none"` (from missing_oracle) and `attrs["divergent_implementation"] == "contradicts_reality"` (unchanged)
decide_ops.py:127 `if attrs.get("ac_unverifiable") in ("missing_oracle", "underspecified_oracle"): attrs["ac_unverifiable"] = "none"` — the broken_oracle exclusion is never asserted
decide_ops.py:133-134 `if attrs.get("divergent_implementation") == "incomplete_enumeration": attrs["divergent_implementation"] = "none"` — this positive-clear branch has no covering assertion
`assert "does not make a completed test run" in body` and `assert "does not make a deployment outcome" in body` are prose phrases, not parsed tokens

The prompt is loaded by prompts.get_prompt and fed to the model; no non-human consumer branches on these sentences (contrast the tag tokens [operator-attested]/[operator_attested] which the regex parses)
advisory.finding: test_exact_tag_semantics_and_pass3_enrichment_remain_fail_safe does not exercise the deliberately-asymmetric enrichment guard branches: the incomplete_enumeration->'none' clear (decide_ops.py:133-134) and the broken_oracle non-clear guard (decide_ops.py:124-127) go untested. A regression that stopped clearing incomplete_enumeration, or that started over-clearing broken_oracle, would not be caught by this suite.
merged_from: test_prompt_distinguishes_related_code_from_external_outcome_evidence asserts exact prose phrases ('does not make a completed test run', 'existence of deployment', etc.) inside an LLM-consumed reviewer prompt .md. Since the consumer is an LLM (not a parser/registry that branches on the exact string), these are wording assertions that would break on a behavior-preserving reword of the prompt without any classifier-behavior change.
scenarios: A future edit that adds 'broken_oracle' to the clear set (over-clearing a factually-wrong stated command)

src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py:404 `"emits_valid_findings": _schema_review_result,`
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py:145-152 `_schema_review_result(_case, out)` ignores `_case` and only calls `validate_result(out)` — no fire/no-fire-by-expectation check
The precision/recall/regression claims therefore rest solely on the hand-recorded docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/evidence_kind_live_eval.json, not on an enforced scorer.
dropped.finding: The eval spec's only gating scorer `emits_valid_findings` resolves to `_schema_review_result`, which validates ONLY the output schema and ignores the case — it does NOT check that a `finding` case emits >=1 evidence-kind finding and a `pass` case emits none. The scorer `description` overstates what is enforced, so the `at_least(2)` gate passes on any schema-valid output regardless of classification correctness.
scenarios: A future prompt regression that misclassifies fixtures still passes the eval as long as output is schema-valid.
CI 'discipline gate' over packaged specs reports the criterion as gated on quality when it is only gated on schema.
